Article Title: Amid opposition walkout, Rajya Sabha gives approval to Vande Mataram bill
Article Text:
File photo: Rajya Sabha proceedings during the Monsoon Session of Parliament

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha on Wednesday passed a bill proposing up to three-year jail term and/or fine for anyone preventing or disturbing the rendition of 'Vande Mataram', even as the opposition benches remained empty in view of almost all opposition MPs staging a walkout.The opposition parties - which included Congress, TMC, DMK, RJD Left, Sena UBT - were pressing their demand for home minister Amit Shah to make a statement on police action against NEET paper leak protesters. Angry MPs stood up and raised slogans. At one point of time, TMC MP Derek O'Brien even rushed towards the deputy chairman Harivansh, to make a point of order, but the Parliament security personnel created a barrier and also stood guard in the well.During the debate, Chair called out to opposition MPs who had given notices to speak, but be it DMK's Tiruchi Siva, TMC's Sagarika Ghose or RJD's Manoj Kumar Jha, they tried to steer the discussion to raising the "brutal force" used on students. Even though the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill is a home ministry bill, it was not Amit Shah but Nityanand Rai who piloted it Wednesday.RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha spoke briefly, questioning the criminalisation of insult to the national song, saying that "reverence cannot be legislated".Junior home minister Nityanand Rai, while replying to the debate, criticised Congress for undermining Vande Mataram and linked it to its policy of appeasement. "Opposing the Vande Mataram amounts to boosting the morale of 'Bharat tere tukde honge' gang," Rai added.AAP didn't walk out with the rest of the opposition, and MP Sanjay Singh spoke during the debate. He questioned "RSS's refusal to hoist the tricolour at its office for 52 years".While BJP MPs welcomed the criminalisation of insults to national song, AIADMK MP criticised the practice in Tamil Nadu to play the state anthem after the national song and the anthem.
Article Summary: Rajya Sabha passed a bill proposing up to three-year jail term and/or fine for anyone preventing or disturbing the rendition of 'Vande Mataram' Opposition benches remained empty in view of almost all opposition MPs staging a walkout. The opposition parties were pressing their demand for home minister Amit Shah to make a statement.

Article Title: Punjab pharmacy exam row: Heavy security outside AAP's Delhi office ahead of BJP protest
Article Text:
Heavy security deployed outside the AAP office as BJP workers are likely to hold the protest over the alleged paper leak in Punjab.





NEW DELHI: Heavy security has been deployed outside the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) headquarters in Delhi ahead of a possible BJP protest over alleged examination paper leaks in Punjab.RAF personnel, Delhi Police personnel and barricades were seen outside the party office on Thursday morning. Traffic movement in the area, however, remained normal at the time of reporting.The protest comes amid a political row over alleged irregularities in recruitment and other examinations in Punjab.Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal on Tuesday alleged that Punjab had witnessed six major paper leaks over the past five years and accused the AAP government of failing to ensure accountability."There have been six major paper leaks in Punjab over the past five years, and several instances of cheating in examinations have come to light. Even on July 19, there was massive cheating in the pharmacy examination. Arvind Kejriwal, who is functioning like a 'super CM' in Punjab, has maintained complete silence on the issue. The Punjab chief minister continues to make irresponsible statements," Maliwal said.She also demanded the resignation of Punjab education minister Harjot Singh Bains and accused AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal of remaining silent on alleged examination irregularities in the state.The controversy follows the July 19 pharmacy officer recruitment examination, during which Punjab Police busted an alleged inter-state cheating racket.Seven alleged masterminds were arrested and 28 candidates were detained after police recovered battery-operated wireless cheating devices, including pen cameras and real-time dictation tools.Police, however, said the investigation found no evidence of a question paper leak or the involvement of any government official.Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann has rejected the opposition's allegations, maintaining that not a single competitive examination paper had leaked during the AAP government's four-and-a-half years in office.He said the pharmacy officer case involved an attempted cheating racket that was detected and foiled by the police.
Article Summary: Heavy security deployed outside the AAP office as BJP workers are likely to hold the protest over the alleged paper leak in Punjab. Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal on Tuesday alleged that Punjab had witnessed six major paper leaks over the past five years. She also demanded the resignation of Punjab education minister Harjot Singh Bains.

Article Title: 60-year-old woman killed by son for refusing to give money for liquor
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A 60-year-old partially handicapped woman was beaten to death allegedly by her son after she refused to give him money to purchase liquor in south Delhi ’s Maidan Garhi on Wednesday. The accused son has been arrested, police said.The deceased woman has been identified as Chinta Devi, a resident of UP Colony in the Kharak Gaon village area. The accused, Amod, is her younger son.Chinta Devi was a housewife who lived with her two sons, elder daughter-in-law and a three-year-old granddaughter. Amod’s wife and child live in Samastipur Vihar.The elderly woman had reportedly turned partially handicapped after an accident in 2013. Her husband is no more. Her elder son works in painting homes, while the accused is a tile contractor.A PCR call was received about the murder at the Maidan Garhi police station. Cops rushed to the spot to find that Chinta Devi was lying injured inside her house. She was rushed to Safdarjung Hospital, where attending doctors declared her brought dead on arrival.A police officer said, “Frequent arguments and assault incidents were reported from the household. We are probing if the accused was under the influence at the time of the incident.”A case was registered and Amod was traced and arrested.
Article Summary: Chinta Devi was a housewife who lived with her two sons, elder daughter-in-law and a three-year-old granddaughter. The elderly woman had reportedly turned partially handicapped after an accident in 2013. Her elder son works in painting homes, while the accused is a tile contractor.

Article Title: Court stays NBW, asks SFI’s Aishe Ghosh to appear today in 2021 protest case
Article Text: New Delhi: A court Wednesday stayed for a day a non-bailable warrant (NBW) issued against SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh in connection with a 2021 protest outside Banga Bhawan in the city.While hearing Ghosh’s application seeking cancellation of the NBW, judicial magistrate first class Vijayshree Rathore noted that she “couldn’t appear on the last date of hearing due to unavoidable circumstances” and asked her to appear Thursday.The warrant, issued on Dec 12, 2024, and again on April 11, 2026, relates to a case in which Ghosh is accused of violating a govt order by participating in a demonstration on Feb 12, 2021. It was organised by Students’ Federation of India and Democratic Youth Federation of India outside Banga Bhawan in Chanakyapuri against police action on protesters in Kolkata opposing Citizenship Amendment Act-National Register of Citizens a day earlier.According to Delhi Police , the protest was held in a prohibited area in violation of prohibitory orders and protesters refused to disperse despite directions. An FIR was registered under sections 188 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant), 34 (common intention) and 447 (criminal trespass) of IPC. A chargesheet was filed in Feb 2022, and arguments on charges are yet to begin.
Article Summary: SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh is accused of violating a govt order by participating in a demonstration on Feb 12, 2021. It was organised by Students’ Federation of India and Democratic Youth Federation. A chargesheet was filed in Feb 2022, and arguments on charges are yet to begin.

Article Title: TET paper leak: Order reserved on bail pleas of 3 accused
Article Text:
So far, 15 persons have been arrested in the case

Bhiwandi:





A Bhiwandi court on Wednesday reserved its order on the bail pleas of three accused in the TET exam leak, including Suman Gupta, wife of alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, till Aug 4.Appearing for the accused, advocate Shailesh Gaikwad said Suman, Sanjay Sharma and Mithun Kumar had no direct role in the paper leak.The prosecution said the allegations are serious and many accused are still absconding. It said granting bail at this stage could hamper the ongoing investigation.Meanwhile, police brought Bijendra back to Bhiwandi after taking him to his hometown in Samastipur district of Bihar and other locations to collect evidence linked to the alleged conspiracy. Sources said police are examining documents, electronic devices and other material. Police have also requested the state govt to appoint a special public prosecutor for the trial.So far, 15 persons have been arrested in the case, including two employees of an Agra-based printing press from where investigators claim the paper was leaked and supplied to the racket.
Article Summary: Bhiwandi court reserved its order on the bail pleas of three accused in the TET exam leak. The prosecution said the allegations are serious and many accused are still absconding. It said granting bail at this stage could hamper the ongoing investigation.

Article Title: Congress stages rasta roko in Kalyan over police action on Jantar Mantar protesters
Article Text:
Congress workers staged a protest in Kalyan West against alleged police action.





KALYAN: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West to protest against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi over the alleged paper leak issue.Led by Navin Singh, Kalyan District President, the protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators by the Delhi Police.Traffic was briefly affected in the area before police intervened.The party also submitted a memorandum to the Kalyan tehsildar, addressed to the President of India, seeking an inquiry into the alleged police action against students and Congress leaders, including Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and other party leaders, during the protest at Delhi.In the memorandum, the Congress demanded the immediate resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, holding him morally responsible for the alleged irregularities in the paper leak. The party also sought an urgent discussion in Parliament on alleged examination irregularities and issues affecting students' future.The memorandum further demanded that all FIRs and criminal cases registered against students and peaceful protesters be withdrawn immediately.Among those present at the protest were corporator Samina Sheikh, former corporator Iftekar Khan and other Congress office-bearers and workers. Police maintained security at the protest site and ensured traffic movement was restored after the demonstration concluded.
Article Summary: Congress workers staged a rasta roko protest at Shivaji Chowk in Kalyan West. They were protesting against the alleged police action on students demonstrating at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The protesters raised slogans against the Centre and demanded action over the alleged assault on students and peaceful demonstrators.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar violence echoes in KDMC house meet as opposition, MNS protest police action
Article Text:
As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House.





KALYAN: The Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation (KDMC) General Body meeting on Thursday witnessed high drama as opposition corporators staged a protest against the alleged police action against students demonstrating at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned to condemn the police action and express solidarity with the injured protesters.As soon as the proceedings began, opposition members stood up, shouted slogans and disrupted the House, forcing Mayor Harshali Chaudhary to adjourn the meeting for 10 minutes.However, after the House reconvened, the opposition continued its protest, condemning what it termed police brutality at Jantar Mantar and urging corporators from the ruling alliance to join them.The protest also witnessed an unusual political alignment, with the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS), a ruling ally of the Shiv Sena in the KDMC, joining hands with the Shiv Sena (UBT) during the demonstration. The BJP took a swipe at the MNS, saying that if MNS corporators wished to sit with the opposition, they should first resign from the ruling alliance and formally move to the opposition benches.Differences within the ruling alliance also came to the fore during the debate. Shiv Sena corporator Mahesh Gaikwad demanded that the House observe a two-minute silence in memory of the students who were allegedly injured in the police action. BJP group leader Shashikant Kamble objected, stating that several police personnel were also injured during the Jantar Mantar protest and that, if a condolence gesture was to be made, it should include them as well.Despite the noisy scenes and repeated slogan-shouting, the General Body meeting continued. Later, leaders of the Shiv Sena and BJP jointly cleared several civic proposals without detailed discussion, while a few agenda items were deferred for consideration at a later meeting.
Article Summary: Corporators from the opposition, including the Shiv Sena (UBT), Congress and NCP (SP), entered the House carrying the Tricolour and wearing black armbands as a mark of protest. Raising slogans of "Bharat Mata Ki Jai" and "Vande Mataram", they demanded that the House be adjourned.

Article Title: BJP-Cong face-off likely during Amit Shah’s visit on Saturday
Article Text:
Ajit Doval (left) and Amit Shah

Pune:





Union home minister Amit Shah ’s visit to Pune on Aug 1 may lead to a face-off with Congress workers calling an agitation to protest Delhi police action at Jantar Mantar during the CJP protest last week and BJP warning that it would hold a counter-stir in such a case.Shah is expected to confer the Lokmanya Tilak National award to national security adviser Ajit Doval on Aug 1 in the city. Congress has decided to use the opportunity to take up the issue of police action against the Jantar Mantar protesters who were then demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.The Pune unit of Congress has sought police permission to stage a protest at Seven Loves Chowk on Saturday. Meanwhile, Pune unit chief of BJP Dheeraj Ghate met police commissioner Amitesh Kumar and submitted a letter, urging him not to grant permission to Congress.Ghate said, “The Union home minister is coming to Pune for the Lokmanya Tilak Award ceremony. It is not a political visit. But Congress is trying to politicise the issue by announcing an agitation against him. We will give a befitting reply if they try to create a ruckus.” BJP warned of a counter-agitation at Seven Loves Chowk if Congress went ahead with its stir on Saturday.Congress’s Pune east chief Prashant Jagtap said, “Our party accepts BJP’s challenge and we are ready for a showdown.Our party is raising its voice against the police brutality against the protesters in Delhi for which Amit Shah is responsible.”If BJP and Congress go ahead with their protests on Aug 1, it would be a repeat of a similar face-off between the two parties three years ago on the same day in Pune. Lokmanya Tilak National Award was conferred on Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Aug 1, 2023, and Congress party workers had protested against the PM with BJP countering the opposition.
Article Summary: Shah is expected to confer the Lokmanya Tilak National award to national security adviser Ajit Doval on Aug 1 in the city. Congress has decided to use the opportunity to take up the issue of police action against the Jantar Mantar protesters who were then demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister.

Article Title: Educationist and BJP functionary arrested in fake Shalarth ID case
Article Text:
A team of Nashik police tak educationist Sanjay Garud into custody from a farmhouse in a village in Solapur district on Monday.

Nashik:





The city police on Monday arrested a well-known educationist from Jalgaon in the fake Shalarth ID case on Monday.The accused has been identified as Sanjay Garud, who is a also a BJP functionary and resident of Shendurni in Jamner taluka of Jalgaon district. This marks the sixth arrest in the case registered with the Nashik Road police station in March this year.An officer from the Nashik city police said 67-year-old Garud was evading arrest. “On Monday, he was arrested from a farmhouse in Natepute in Solapur district in connection with the case registered on March 12, 2026, for offences punishable under Sections 318(4) (Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property), 316(2) (criminal breach of trust), 316(5) (covering specific breach of trust), 336(2)(3) (forgery of documents or electronic record) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy to commit serious offence) among other sections of the BNS and the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000. ”ACP (crime) Sandeep Mitke said the scam involves systematic embezzlement of govt funds amounting to Rs160 crore under the jurisdiction of deputy director of education (Nashik division), covering Nashik, Jalgaon, Dhule and Nandurbar districts.He said a total of 841 teaching and non-teaching staff members were illegally included into the official ‘Shalarth’ salary system. Without submitting the mandatory individual approval proposals to the education department, the accused forged backdated appointment orders and drafted fraudulent entries into the payroll software to siphon off monthly salaries and arrear payments.So far, around 1,200 individuals, including school principals, trust operators, former deputy directors of education, education officers and pay superintendents, have been identified as suspects.Sanjay Garud operates 15 school institutions. The investigation by the Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by Mitke has found that fake individual approvals were issued for 177 staff members across his schools, even though no valid approval proposals were ever received or processed by the education officer’s department.Following confidential intelligence and precise technical tracking, the Nashik crime branch discovered that Garud was taking refuge at a farmhouse in Solapur. Under the guidance of Mitke, a specialised team comprising sub-inspector Chetan Shrivant and officers Pravin Waghmare, Mahesh Salunkhe, Uttam Pawar, Milindsingh Pardeshi and Nazim Khan Pathan raided the location.On being asked about the arrest, water resources minister Girish Mahajan said he was taking information about the same.
Article Summary: The accused has been identified as Sanjay Garud, a also a BJP functionary and resident of Shendurni in Jamner taluka of Jalgaon district. This marks the sixth arrest in the case registered with the Nashik Road police station in March this year.

Article Title: Madras high court rejects anticipatory bail plea of DMK MLA V Senthilbalaji in 'corruption' case
Article Text: CHENNAI: The Madras high court on Thursday dismissed the anticipatory bail plea filed by DMK MLA and former minister V Senthilbalaji in connection with a corruption case registered against him by the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC).The court observed that the allegations against Senthilbalaji involved causing a loss of over Rs 17 crore to the public exchequer and held that the case required custodial interrogation of the accused."The allegation was of having caused a loss of over Rs 17 crore to the public exchequer and therefore, the case requires custodial interrogation of the accused," the high court said.The case was registered by the DVAC against Senthilbalaji over allegations of corruption.The DMK leader had approached the court seeking protection from arrest through an anticipatory bail plea.
Article Summary: The case was registered by the DVAC against Senthilbalaji over allegations of corruption. The DMK leader had approached the court seeking protection from arrest through an anticipatory bail plea. The allegation was of having caused a loss of over Rs 17 crore to the public exchequer.

Article Title: Three women from MP arrested for stealing jewellery, cash from shoppers in T Nagar
Article Text:
Busted

Chennai:





Mambalam police arrested three women from Madhya Pradesh for stealing jewellery and cash from shoppers at a commercial establishments in T Nagar. Police recovered ₹6.44lakh in cash from them.The accused were identified as Lakshmibai , 40, Meenakshi, 35, and Khushbu , 40, all from Rajgarh district in Madhya Pradesh.On July 25, a woman shopping at a jewellery showroom on Usman Road reported that four sovereigns of gold jewellery had been stolen from her handbag. On the same day, a Sri Lankan national lodged a complaint alleging that ₹75,000 in cash and an ATM card were stolen while he was shopping at a textile store in T Nagar.With the help of CCTV footage, Mambalam police identified the suspects and tracked them to Puducherry . Meanwhile, the Puducherry police had already arrested the three while targeting another customer. They were remanded to judicial custody at Puzhal Central PrisonAn investigation revealed the women operated across Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad, distracting customers before stealing valuables. Lakshmibai had five prior criminal cases, and Meenakshi and Khushbu had four each. Further investigations are on.
Article Summary: Mambalam police arrested three women from Madhya Pradesh for stealing jewellery and cash from shoppers at a commercial establishments in T Nagar. The accused were identified as Lakshmibai, 40, Meenakshi, 35, and Khushbu, 40. Police recovered ₹6.44lakh in cash from them. They were remanded to judicial custody at Puzhal Central Prison.

Article Title: Sengottaiyan flays previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies on Mekedatu dam issue
Article Text:
K A Sengottaiyan





ERODE: Tamil Nadu revenue minister K A Sengottaiyan on Saturday criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu.Speaking at a consultation meeting of officials from different departments held at the Erode district collectorate, Sengottaiyan reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move to build a dam in Mekedatu.During the review meeting, the minister told officials to deliver results quickly, saying the govt’s performance since coming to power warranted a thorough review and that the people’s demands should be met without delay. “Officers must complete necessary office procedures promptly and ensure citizens receive timely relief,” he told reporters after the meeting.The review, chaired by district collector S Kandasamy and also attended by handloom minister M Vijay Balaji, covered a wide range of administrative concerns.A major focus was the Athikadavu-Avinashi integrated drinking water project. Officials were directed to find out why more than 70 ponds were not getting filled and asked them to take remedial measures. Officials were instructed to begin silt-removal operations in the Bhavanisagar Dam to improve storage capacity and downstream supply.On allegations that liquor outlets were operating in violation of regulations, the revenue minister demanded concrete statistics and warned that strict action would follow where breaches were confirmed.
Article Summary: K A Sengottaiyan criticized the previous DMK govt for not having pursued legal remedies to stop Karnataka’s move to build a dam across the Cauvery river in Mekedatu. He reiterated that chief minister C Joseph Vijay had urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to halt the move.

Article Title: Palani Mutt temple land case: CB-CID arrests 3 over Rs 100 crore property fraud
Article Text: DINDIGUL: The CB-CID has arrested three persons on Wednesday morning in connection with the case pertaining to fraudulent registration of the 1.4-acre land valued at Rs 100 crore, belonging to the Arulmigu Dhandapani Swamigal Madam in Palani in Dindigul district.The arrested were identified as Murugadas, 56, of Villupuram, who allegedly sold the land using forged documents; Vellaithurai,60, of Tiruppur, who allegedly purchased the property; and advocate Anwardeen,65, of Palani, who is suspected to have facilitated the transaction.Cases have been registered against them under sections 318(4), 336(3), 340(2), 49 and 61(2) of BNS..The case pertains to the alleged fraudulent registration of mutt land, valued at around Rs 100 crore through fabricated records.Following a complaint lodged by Muruganandam, superintendent of the Palani temple lands division, the Palani Adivaram police had initially registered a case against former sub-registrar Justin Manikandan, trust functionary Murugadas, purchaser Vellaithurai and Sethupathi of Palani Pudur under various charges, including cheating and criminal conspiracy.The Tamil Nadu government transferred the investigation to the CB-CID on July 15.A special team led by CB-CID SP B H Sajitha and DSP Ajay Thangam has since been conducting an extensive inquiry in Dindigul and Palani.More than 15 persons, including former temple joint commissioner Marimuthu, retired tahsildar Mariyappan, retired village administrative officer Chinnasamy, and HR&CE inspector Sivanesan, have been questioned.
Article Summary: The case pertains to the alleged fraudulent registration of mutt land, valued at around Rs 100 crore through fabricated records. More than 15 persons, including former temple joint commissioner Marimuthu, retired tahsildar Mariyappan, retired village administrative officer Chinnasamy, and HR&CE inspector Sivanesan have been questioned.

Article Title: Fireman dies by suicide alleging harassment by loan sharks in Madurai; one arrested
Article Text:
Madurai

:





Police arrested a man in connection with the alleged abetment of suicide of a fire and rescue services personnel who was found hanging at his house in Usilampatti in Madurai district on Saturday.The deceased, identified as Sureshkumar, a resident of Sathya Nagar in Usilampatti, was serving as a fireman at the Guindy Fire and Rescue Services Station in Chennai. He came to his native place on leave when he allegedly died by suicide at his residence.According to police sources, before taking the extreme step, Sureshkumar recorded and released a video stating that he had borrowed more than Rs5 lakh on interest and was facing persistent harassment from lenders.Based on the contents of the video and subsequent investigation, Usilampatti Town Police registered a case and arrested Praveenkumar, from Nalliveeranpatti, on Monday, who is alleged to have lent money to the deceased.Police have registered a case against Praveenkumar under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Further investigation is under way to ascertain the circumstances that led to Sureshkumar's death and whether others were involved in the alleged harassment.(Assistance for those having suicidal thoughts is available on TN’s health helpline 104 and Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050)
Article Summary: The deceased, identified as Sureshkumar, was serving as a fireman at the Guindy Fire and Rescue Services Station in Chennai. He came to his native place on leave when he allegedly died by suicide at his residence. Police have registered a case against Praveenkumar under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.

Article Title: Kerala Police Association moves HC against order for membership tweak
Article Text:
Kochi

:





Kerala Police Association, an association representing police personnel in the ranks of civil police officer and senior civil police officer, has filed a petition before the high court challenging a govt order directing the reorganisation of its membership.The additional chief secretary, home, issued the order on July 27, directing the association to reorganise its membership to include all civil police officers, senior civil police officers, grade assistant sub inspectors, assistant sub inspectors and grade sub inspectors. It further directed that officers from the rank of sub inspector up to superintendent of police (non-IPS) be included in the Kerala Police Senior Officers Association (KPSOA). According to the order, the state police chief shall constitute an ad hoc committee at the state level and similar committees in all districts. It also directed that all elected committees of the association be frozen and that the ad hoc committees take over its administration.The petitioners contended that the reorganisation of the police associations and the abolition of one of the associations, which has been functioning for the past 47 years, were carried out without any justification. They further contended that, under Article 33 of the Constitution, the power to modify the rights conferred on members of the armed forces and the forces charged with the maintenance of public order vests exclusively in Parliament. Therefore, the state govt and its officers cannot encroach upon powers exclusively vested in Parliament under the Constitution, they argued. The court is scheduled to consider the petition on Thursday.
Article Summary: Kerala Police Association has filed a petition before the high court challenging a govt order directing the reorganisation of its membership. The additional chief secretary, home, issued the order on July 27, directing the association to reorganise its membership to include all civil police officers. The court is scheduled to consider the petition on Thursday.
